title: The first crib (Greccio, 1223)
hookLine: Francis sets up a manger with an ox and donkey so people can see

cards: A bundle of hay. An ox. A donkey.

A rough wooden feeding trough in a hillside village called Greccio, in the middle of a winter night. People climb up from the farms with candles and torches, and the woods fill with light and singing.

In Celano's telling no one lays a baby in the straw. There's a manger, two animals breathing in the cold, and a small man in a patched habit, overflowing with joy. Francis of Assisi has asked a friend to build this.

teach.h: HE WANTED TO SEE IT WITH HIS EYES.
teach.b: Thomas of Celano, who wrote an early life of Francis, says Francis wanted to see with his own eyes how the child of Bethlehem had lain in a manger, the hardship of it, the ox and the ass standing by.
He had heard the Christmas story all his life. He wanted the village to see it, not only hear it.
The Gospel line he had in mind is Luke's, which in the Douay-Rheims reads: "and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn." The animals aren't in Luke.

teach.h: THE OX AND ASS COME FROM ISAIAH.
teach.b: They come from the prophet Isaiah: "The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib." A beast, the prophet says, knows where its food comes from.
Tradition placed those two beside the manger, and Francis put real ones there.
A priest celebrated Mass right over the manger.

Francis, who was a deacon and never a priest, sang the Gospel and preached, and Celano says he called Jesus the child of Bethlehem, saying the word Bethlehem so tenderly it sounded like a lamb's bleat.

Celano adds that one man there saw a child lying in the manger as if asleep, and Francis seemed to wake him. Celano doesn't call Greccio the first of anything; first is the title tradition gave it later.

teach.h: NO ROOM FOR THEM IN THE INN.
teach.b: What Greccio gave was a habit. Catholic homes and parishes still set out a crib in Advent, with an ox and a donkey nearby. A faith you can stand in front of, and see.

how: Catholic families and parishes set up a crib, or nativity scene, for Advent and Christmas; some wait until Christmas Eve to lay the figure of the child in the manger.

practice: Choose one small thing that keeps your faith, or whatever you hold dear, in sight: a crucifix moved to where you'll pass it, a holy card, a candle, a photo of someone you pray for or simply love.
Picture it in its place and look at it the way the people at Greccio looked at the manger. If you pray, let the sight of it be the prayer.

wordCard.voice: Greccio. The hillside village where Francis set out a manger with an ox and a donkey so people could see the Christmas story. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: a manger or crib, the word Luke's Gospel uses in the Latin Bible.
